title: going to para planes
short: I'm going to visit my son. Para planes ya decididos: am / is / are + going to + verbo.

story.title: Ya lo has decidido
story.text: Para contar un plan que ya tienes pensado usamos ==going to==. Es como nuestro «voy a»: I'm going to travel = voy a viajar.

examples.t: I'm going to visit my son in May.
examples.es: Voy a visitar a mi hijo en mayo.

examples.t: We're going to travel by train.

story.title: Las cuatro formas
story.text: Solo cambia el verbo ==to be== (am, is, are). Going to y el verbo de después no cambian nunca.

head: Afirmativa
Negativa
Pregunta
Respuesta corta
rows: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.
Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.

story.title: Tres piezas
story.text: ==am / is / are== + going to + ==verbo base==. Sin -s, sin -ing, sin pasado: She's going to ==visit== (no visits).

examples.t: My friend is going to come with me.
examples.es: Mi amiga va a venir conmigo.

examples.t: Are you going to book the hotel?

story.title: Predecir con pruebas
story.text: También usamos going to cuando ==vemos== que algo va a pasar: hay nubes negras, el autobús va lleno…

examples.t: Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.

story.title: I'm going to go: ¡correcto!
story.text: Aunque suene repetido, ==I'm going to go== está bien: es «voy a ir». Con ir, también se puede acortar: I'm going to London in May.

examples.t: I'm going to go to Oxford.

story.title: Casi igual que en español
story.text: Voy a viajar = I'm going to travel. Las dos diferencias: hace falta ==am / is / are== y no te olvides del ==to==.

story.title: Errores típicos
story.text:
❌ I going to travel. ✅ I=='m== going to travel.
❌ She's going to visits. ✅ She's going to ==visit==.
❌ We're going travel. ✅ We're going ==to== travel.

story.title: Oído: gonna
story.text: En conversación rápida, going to suena ==«gona»== y a veces se escribe gonna. Reconócelo en series y canciones, pero tú escribe siempre ==going to==.

compare.es: En español decimos «voy a + infinitivo» para planes: voy a viajar, vamos a comer fuera.
compare.target: En inglés es muy parecido: am / is / are + going to + verbo base. No olvides el verbo to be ni el to: I'm going to travel.

errors.wrong: I going to visit my sister.
errors.right: I'm going to visit my sister.
errors.why: Falta el verbo to be: I'm (I am) going to.

errors.wrong: She's going to visits her mum.
errors.right: She's going to visit her mum.
errors.why: Después de going to, el verbo en forma base, sin -s.

errors.right: We're going to travel by train.
errors.why: No te comas el to: going to travel.

errors.wrong: I go to visit my son next week.
errors.right: I'm going to visit my son next week.
errors.why: «Voy a» no es I go to: es I'm going to.

errors.wrong: I will visit my son in May. (ya tengo los billetes)
errors.right: I'm going to visit my son in May.
errors.why: Para planes ya decididos lo natural es going to.

exercises.q: I ___ going to visit my son in May.

exercises.why: My friend = she: is going to.

exercises.why: Después de going to, verbo base: take.

exercises.q: Look at those clouds! It's going to ___.
exercises.why: Predicción con pruebas: going to + rain.

She ___ going to cook paella on Sunday.

exercises.q: We ___ going to travel in August. It's too hot.
exercises.es: No vamos a viajar en agosto. Hace demasiado calor.
answer: aren't
are not
exercises.why: Negativa con we: aren't going to.

answer: Are

exercises.q: What are you going to ___ in London?
answer: do

exercises.q: I'm going to ___ a big suitcase.

bring

exercises.q: Is your friend going to come? — Yes, she ___.

answer: is
exercises.why: My grandson = he: is going to.

exercises.q: They ___ going to visit us at Easter.
answer: are

answer: I'm not
I am not

She is not going to drive to Madrid.

answer: Are they going to stay with us?
